title: TS SDK: checkpointed streaming adapter for graceful reconnect and interop
creator: Asha Khanna
description: Implement a TypeScript SDK streaming adapter that attaches lightweight checkpoint markers to streamed payloads so clients can gracefully reconnect and resume consumption across transient network failures while maintaining compatibility with both AsyncIterator and Web Streams consumer patterns.
background: Customers building chat and long-response features report brittle streaming behavior when mobile networks drop or when browser tabs are suspended. Current SDK approaches either (a) expose raw Web Streams/AsyncIterator semantics but expect app-level resume logic, or (b) force a single consumer model that doesn't map well across Node/browser runtimes. We need a developer-friendly primitive that: allows resume without re-requesting full context, cooperates with backpressure, and remains ergonomic for both AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumers.
proposal: Add a 'checkpointed' stream layer in the TypeScript SDK that embeds periodic opaque checkpoint tokens into the metadata stream (not the user-visible tokens) and exposes a resumeHandshake API. Key pieces: 1) Checkpoint token format (opaque base64 string containing sequence id + KV-checksum + server nonce); 2) SDK-side buffering and watermarks to ensure checkpoints are emitted only at stable commit points; 3) Resume handshake that validates last-seen checkpoint and tail-replays only missing deltas; 4) Dual consumer facade: a ReadableStream wrapper plus an AsyncIterator adapter that share the same checkpointing state and backpressure signals; 5) Telemetry hooks for resume attempts, missed-checkpoint rates, and bytes-replayed in console traces.
tradeoffs: Pros: improves mobile/edge UX, reduces user-perceived failure, can cut bandwidth for large generated responses. Cons: increases server-side state complexity for resume windows, requires changes to protocol for checkpoint tokens (backwards compatibility via opt-in request flag), slightly more memory pressure in SDK due to short replay buffers. We avoid full persistent session state by bounding replay window to configurable token count or byte size. Rollout can be opt-in per-client-version to avoid immediate server-side burden.
implementation_plan: Design checkpoint token schema and document in design doc (drive: /design/ts-checkpointed-streaming.md)
Implement SDK encoder/decoder for checkpoint tokens and small in-memory replay buffer (ts/sdk/stream/checkpoint.ts)
Add ReadableStream wrapper that emits internal metadata chunk for checkpoints and keeps user-facing stream clean
Add AsyncIterator adapter that reuses same underlying buffer and exposes resumeCursor() to client code
Server-side minimal support: accept resume tokens and return delta frames (server PR: GH#12567) - coordinate with serving/runtime team
Integrate telemetry events: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_fail, bytes_replayed
Add unit and e2e tests for resume success, mismatched token, window-expired replay, and backpressure scenarios
Docs: examples for browser and Node, migration guide, and API surface in SDK README
testing_plan: Unit tests for token encode/decode and checksum verification
Fake server harness that simulates mid-stream disconnect and verifies resume handshake replays only missing frames
Stress test with concurrent reconnects and verify server's bounded memory behavior
Browser integration tests: ensure ReadableStream consumers receive identical bytes post-resume and that streams close cleanly on cancellation
Type-level tests for AsyncIterator/ReadableStream dual-consumer types to ensure ergonomics across TS configs
Load test on dedicated staging to measure additional latency introduced by checkpoint scaffolding
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes CheckpointedStream and resumeHandshake APIs with clear examples
A reconnect test demonstrates resume within configured replay window (<= 5s window in default) without duplicating tokens to user callbacks
Backpressure is preserved: a slow consumer does not cause unbounded buffering on resume path
Telemetry metrics surface resume success/failure in Console dashboard (trace links present)
PRs merged for SDK and server-side minimal resume endpoint with opt-in flag
TypeScript typings pass internal lint and CI builds across Node 18+ and browser targets
